title: M3C2 Level of Detection (95% Confidence)

σ_reg.description: Registration error between epochs (from ICP RMS or GCP residuals)

σ₁.description: Surface roughness (standard deviation of points from local plane) in epoch 1

n₁, n₂.description: Number of points within projection cylinder for each epoch

applicability: Per-point detection limit. Roughness and density vary spatially — LOD is not constant. Smooth surfaces with high density achieve LOD < 5 mm. Rough surfaces (rubble, vegetation) may have LOD > 50 mm.

title: DEM of Difference (DoD)
applicability: Positive values = surface rise (deposition, heave, swelling). Negative values = surface lowering (erosion, settlement, excavation). Both DEMs must be in the same coordinate system and datum.
source: Wheaton et al. (2010), general geomorphic change detection

title: DoD Uncertainty Propagation
applicability: Assumes errors in the two DEMs are uncorrelated (valid for independent surveys). If systematic errors exist (e.g., same GPS base station), correlation reduces effective uncertainty. Spatially variable σ_DEM enables cell-by-cell LOD.
source: Brasington et al. (2003), Wheaton et al. (2010)

title: Volumetric Change from DoD
equation: ΔV = Σᵢ [DoD(i) × A_cell]  for all cells where |DoD(i)| > LOD

ΔV.description: Net volumetric change (positive = net gain, negative = net loss)

applicability: Only sum cells exceeding LOD threshold to avoid noise contamination of volume estimate. Volume uncertainty: σ_V = A_cell × √(Σ σ_DoD(i)²) or approximated as σ_V ≈ σ_DoD_mean × √(N_cells) × A_cell.
source: Wheaton et al. (2010), Lane et al. (2003)

title: Stockpile Volume (Above Base Plane)
equation: V_stockpile = Σᵢ max(0, Z_surface(i) - Z_base(i)) × A_cell

V_stockpile.description: Volume of material above reference base

Z_base.description: Base reference elevation (ground plane or pre-stockpile surface)

applicability: Base surface definition critical. For conical/pyramidal stockpiles, base plane from perimeter toe points. Volume uncertainty dominated by base plane uncertainty at perimeter and surface accuracy at crest. Typical accuracy: 2–5% of volume for well-controlled surveys.

title: Displacement Rate from Multi-Epoch Comparison
applicability: Linear rate assumption valid for steady-state processes. For accelerating movements (landslides approaching failure), fit exponential or inverse-velocity models to multi-epoch data. Velocity precision = displacement precision / time interval.

title: Inverse Velocity Method — Failure Prediction

a, b.description: Linear regression parameters on 1/v vs time plot

applicability: Fukuzono (1985) method adapted for remote sensing. Plot inverse velocity over time; linear trend extrapolated to zero predicts failure time. Requires at least 3 epochs showing acceleration. Works for landslides and some structural failures. Not always linear — can be concave or convex.
source: Fukuzono (1985), adapted for InSAR/LiDAR by Carlà et al. (2017)

title: Area-Based Image Correlation (PIV) Precision

C.description: Correlation quality factor (5–20 for good texture)

applicability: Sub-pixel precision achievable: typically 0.1–0.5 × GSD. With 2 cm GSD UAS imagery, displacement precision of 2–10 mm is typical. Requires good surface texture (natural or applied targets). Poor texture (uniform surfaces) degrades precision significantly.
source: White et al. (2003), Travelletti et al. (2012)
